questions.stem: This schematic maps the sites of action of antiplatelet drugs on an activating platelet. One class acts at the receptor mediating the final common step of platelet aggregation, where the receptor cross-links platelets by binding fibrinogen. Which drug class acts at that final receptor?

explanation.summary: The GP IIb/IIIa receptor binds fibrinogen to cross-link adjacent platelets, the final common pathway of aggregation; agents such as abciximab, eptifibatide, and tirofiban block it. Aspirin acts upstream on COX/thromboxane, and clopidogrel/ticagrelor act on the P2Y12 ADP receptor.
explanation.whyCorrect: The GP IIb/IIIa receptor binds fibrinogen to cross-link adjacent platelets, the final common pathway of aggregation; agents such as abciximab, eptifibatide, and tirofiban block it. Aspirin acts upstream on COX/thromboxane, and clopidogrel/ticagrelor act on the P2Y12 ADP receptor.

questions.stem: The red tracing shows the effect of a Class IA antiarrhythmic on the ventricular action potential compared with normal. What ECG change would this altered action potential most likely produce?

explanation.summary: Class IA agents block Na+ (slowing phase 0) and K+ channels (delaying phase 3), lengthening action potential duration and repolarization, which prolongs the QT interval and predisposes to torsades de pointes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Class IA agents block Na+ (slowing phase 0) and K+ channels (delaying phase 3), lengthening action potential duration and repolarization, which prolongs the QT interval and predisposes to torsades de pointes.

questions.stem: This tracing shows a small change in phase 0 with a shortened action potential, typical of Class IB agents. These drugs preferentially bind sodium channels in myocardium that is in what condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ischemic tissue rich in inactivated channels

explanation.summary: Class IB drugs (e.g., lidocaine) are selective for inactivated Na+ channels, which are abundant in depolarized ischemic myocardium, making them drugs of choice for ventricular arrhythmias after MI.
explanation.whyCorrect: Class IB drugs (e.g., lidocaine) are selective for inactivated Na+ channels, which are abundant in depolarized ischemic myocardium, making them drugs of choice for ventricular arrhythmias after MI.

questions.stem: The red tracing shows pronounced blunting of the phase 0 upstroke while action potential duration is unchanged, typical of Class IC agents. Which ECG finding results?

choices.label: D
choices.text: QT prolongation with a normal QRS

choices.label: E
choices.text: Marked QRS widening with unchanged QT

explanation.summary: Class IC drugs strongly slow phase 0 (conduction velocity) without altering repolarization, so the QRS widens markedly while the QT interval stays essentially unchanged.
explanation.whyCorrect: Class IC drugs strongly slow phase 0 (conduction velocity) without altering repolarization, so the QRS widens markedly while the QT interval stays essentially unchanged.

questions.stem: This stepwise algorithm for managing chronic systolic heart failure separates the numbered core therapies from a side branch (loop diuretics). What best explains why the loop diuretic branch is set apart?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loop diuretics are the mandatory first step before any other agent

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loop diuretics replace the need for an MRA in every patient

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loop diuretics are used only in preserved-EF (diastolic) heart failure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loop diuretics relieve congestive symptoms but do not reduce mortality

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loop diuretics reduce cardiac remodeling and improve survival

explanation.summary: The numbered core agents (ACEi/ARB or ARNI plus beta-blocker, then SGLT2 inhibitor, then MRA) are shown driving the mortality and morbidity benefit. Loop diuretics are added at any step based on signs and symptoms of congestion; they are for symptom control and do not reduce mortality.
explanation.whyCorrect: The numbered core agents (ACEi/ARB or ARNI plus beta-blocker, then SGLT2 inhibitor, then MRA) are shown driving the mortality and morbidity benefit. Loop diuretics are added at any step based on signs and symptoms of congestion; they are for symptom control and do not reduce mortality.
